items.answer: An extended reality system is an interactive system that comprises hardware, an XR engine as middleware, and the application layer, in which input devices track the user's actions and positions, send them as input data, the data is processed to render an environment, and output devices stimulate the user's senses.

Augmented reality (AR) is an enhanced version of reality created by technology, in which computer-generated digital content is overlaid on the real world in real time and registered in 3D, so the user perceives and interacts with the enhanced environment.

Immersive technology is a technology that produces an experience in which a person perceives an environment through sensory organs as real, so that they cannot distinguish it from their real environment.

Digital heritage preservation is the process of using digital media to preserve cultural, educational, scientific, ecological, or other heritage by archiving, digitizing, and using immersive technologies such as virtual reality and augmented reality, allowing virtual exploration of heritage places that cannot be physically visited by large numbers of users or in all parts.

Virtual reality (VR) is an artificial environment experienced through sensory stimuli provided by a computer, in which a person's actions partially determine what happens and which replaces the user's sense of reality without requiring the physical existence of objects or places.

Virtual environment is a non-real, computer-generated graphical representation of a real or imaginary world, populated with artificial objects, that is experienced through computer-generated sensory stimuli.

questions.question: Which existing system development lifecycle is essentially followed to build extended reality systems?
options: The interactive system development lifecycle
The virtual reality system development lifecycle
The augmented reality system development lifecycle
The mixed reality system development lifecycle
questions.explanation: Extended reality systems are examples of interactive systems, so the interactive system development lifecycle can be followed for them. Treating them by a separate virtual, augmented, or mixed reality lifecycle is not supported.

questions.question: In the Majuli case study, what role does the virtual reality system have?
options: It digitally preserves the island's ecological and cultural heritage
It digitally restores the island's eroded habitable areas
It digitally archives the island's traditional preservation methods
It digitally recreates the island's monsoon season in real time
questions.explanation: The case study focuses on a virtual reality system that digitally preserves Majuli's ecological and cultural heritage. It is not mainly about restoring eroded land, recreating weather, or archiving traditional preservation methods.

data.text: Extended reality systems are treated as interactive systems, so their development can follow the same lifecycle used for interactive systems. The Majuli case study gives a concrete preservation problem: the heritage of Majuli River Island. It applies this lifecycle through designing, implementing, and evaluating a VR system that digitally preserves the island's ecological and cultural heritage.
points: Extended reality systems are interactive systems, so the interactive system development lifecycle can essentially be followed to build them.
The Majuli case study develops a VR system to digitally preserve the ecological and cultural heritage of Majuli River Island.

questions.question: Which feature of Majuli is best described as intangible heritage?
options: Skills, knowledge, and aesthetic norms
Satras, tribal homes, and artifacts
Flora, fauna, and island geology
Masks, instruments, and Satra buildings
questions.explanation: Intangible heritage on Majuli includes skills, knowledge, and aesthetic norms that can be sensed but not touched, while artifacts, buildings, and ecological features are tangible or ecological heritage.

questions.question: What makes Majuli's ecological heritage distinctive?
options: Images and videos from the island's digital preservation
Satras and tribal homes from the island's settlement history
Flora and fauna from the island's natural physical setting
Artifacts and instruments from the island's cultural practices
questions.explanation: Majuli's ecological heritage is the flora and fauna tied to the island's naturally formed physical setting, not its cultural artifacts, buildings, or digital records.

questions.question: What does river erosion turn formerly habitable parts of Majuli into?
options: Sandbars, river banks, underwater areas, and barren areas
Museums, archives, virtual tours, and heritage site areas
Farms, orchards, forests, and wildlife sanctuary areas
Villages, Satras, tribal homes, and market areas
questions.explanation: River erosion consumes formerly habitable parts of Majuli, leaving sandbars, river banks, underwater areas, or barren areas rather than new settlements, productive land, or heritage facilities.

questions.question: What role do Satras play in Majuli's cultural heritage?
options: Museums that display artifact and architectural arts
Living workshops that sustain visual and performing arts
Offices that organize ritual and festival arts
Studios that produce pottery and boat-building arts
questions.explanation: Satras are living workshops of visual and performing arts, so their heritage role is sustaining those art forms rather than functioning as museums, craft studios, or administrative offices.

data.text: Majuli is presented as an inhabited river island whose cultural and ecological value is under threat. Floods and erosion have repeatedly reduced the island's area, endangering both its physical existence and its heritage. Its Satras, tribal communities, tangible and intangible heritage, and ecological heritage therefore make preservation urgent.
points: Majuli is the world's largest inhabited river island in Assam and a potential UNESCO site.
Severe annual floods and river erosion have greatly reduced Majuli's land and habitable area, risking disappearance.
Majuli's cultural setting includes Vaishnavite Satras and distinctive tribal communities such as Mising, Deori, and Sonowal Kachari.
Majuli's heritage includes tangible artifacts and architecture, intangible practices, and ecological flora and fauna.
Majuli's tangible, intangible, and ecological heritage must be preserved before the island disappears.

questions.question: What distinguishes digital heritage preservation from traditional cultural-heritage preservation?
options: Use of site maintenance to protect heritage from decay
Use of oral traditions to transmit heritage across generations
Use of digital media to archive and recreate heritage
Use of museums to display heritage objects to visitors
questions.explanation: Digital heritage preservation uses digital media, including archiving and immersive recreation, while traditional preservation relies on methods such as oral traditions, museums, and site maintenance. The wrong options name traditional methods rather than the digital medium.

questions.question: In digital heritage preservation, what does archiving involve?
options: Recreating physical spaces as interactive virtual worlds that users can enter
Letting global audiences explore heritage without visiting the physical site
Storing visual and audio files that capture heritage information
Making digital avatars of fragile objects that may not survive over time
questions.explanation: Archiving is the storage of visual and audio files that capture heritage information. The other options describe immersive recreation, remote access, and digital avatars, not archiving itself.

questions.question: What can a global audience do with immersive heritage technology?
options: Maintain the heritage sites on the island
Replace oral traditions with recorded tours
Explore heritage remotely from home
Create avatars of fragile heritage artifacts
questions.explanation: Immersive technology lets a global audience explore heritage sites, artifacts, and intangible cultural aspects remotely. The other options describe preservation or maintenance tasks that are not the audience's remote experience.

questions.question: Why are digital avatars useful for fragile heritage objects?
options: They can replace the need to maintain historical sites
They can allow visitors to handle the original fragile objects
They can preserve objects that may not survive the passage of time
They can stop the original objects from aging through contact
questions.explanation: Digital avatars can preserve fragile artifacts that may not survive over time. They do not physically stop the original objects from aging, replace site maintenance, or let visitors handle the originals.

data.text: Traditional heritage preservation and digital heritage preservation are different approaches to keeping heritage. Traditional methods use oral traditions, museums, maintenance of historical sites, and documentation, while digital heritage preservation stores visual and audio files, digitizes heritage, and can use immersive technologies. VR is useful because it can recreate physical spaces as virtual worlds, allow interaction when properly designed, and let people explore heritage remotely, while also helping preserve fragile heritage for future generations.
points: Traditional heritage preservation uses oral traditions, museums, maintenance of historical sites, and documentation.
Digital preservation is the use of digital media to preserve educational, scientific, and other resources.
Digital heritage preservation archives visual and audio files, digitizes heritage, and uses immersive technologies such as VR or AR.
VR can recreate physical spaces as virtual worlds and, if properly designed, let users interact with them.
VR can preserve heritage for future generations by creating digital avatars of fragile artifacts and enabling global remote exploration.

questions.question: What are the two clear-cut goals of the Majuli River Island VR system?
options: Heritage preservation and global heritage experience
Erosion documentation and travel service marketing
Tourism promotion and sustainable local economic development
Research advancement and commercial product creation
questions.explanation: The system's two clear-cut goals are preserving heritage and letting users anywhere on Earth experience that heritage. Tourism, research, commercial products, or erosion documentation are not the stated goals of the system.

questions.question: What does heritage preservation mean in the Majuli River Island VR system?
options: Creating a multimedia archive of the island's heritage
Providing a multimedia virtual tour of the island's heritage
Building a multimedia virtual environment of the island's heritage
Creating a multimedia video of the island's heritage
questions.explanation: Heritage preservation in this VR system means creating an archive of heritage information, ideally as a multimedia archive. A virtual tour, a single video, or a virtual environment is not the preservation function itself.

questions.question: What form does heritage experience take in the Majuli River Island VR system?
options: An immersive virtual tour of the island that uses the archive
A non-immersive web gallery of the island that uses the archive
A guided audio visit to the island that uses the archive
A gaming world of the island that uses the archive
questions.explanation: Experiencing the heritage is intended as an immersive virtual tour or exploration of Majuli that uses the heritage archive. A web gallery, audio visit, or gaming world is not the intended form of the heritage experience.

data.text: The Majuli River Island VR system is defined by two linked goals. Preservation creates a multimedia archive of heritage information, and experience uses that archive for an immersive virtual tour of Majuli. This lets the heritage be kept and also explored by users anywhere.
points: The Majuli River Island VR system has two goals: to preserve heritage and let users anywhere experience it.
The Majuli River Island VR system's preservation goal is a multimedia archive of 2D/360-degree images, videos, audio, and text.
The Majuli River Island VR system's experience goal is an immersive virtual tour of Majuli using that archive.

questions.question: Why does the Majuli River Island case study pair a heritage-preservation purpose with a remote-experience purpose?
questions.reference_answer: Severe annual floods and erosion endanger Majuli's cultural resources and material existence, and there is a real possibility that the island may disappear, so its tangible, intangible, and ecological heritage must be preserved. The system's two clear-cut goals are to preserve heritage and to let users anywhere on Earth experience that heritage. Virtual reality supports the remote-experience goal because it permits a global audience to explore heritage sites, artifacts, and intangible aspects of culture remotely from home.

questions.question: How can a virtual reality system for Majuli River Island preserve heritage that is not only physical but also embedded in daily and occasional practices?
questions.reference_answer: It can archive tangible heritage such as masks, musical instruments, and the architecture of Satras and traditional tribal homes as images, videos, audio, and text. It can also use virtual reality as an immersive technology to recreate Majuli River Island as a virtual world, and, if properly designed, let users interact with it. This can present intangible heritage that is typically embedded in daily or occasional activities such as music, dance, drama, and mask making.

questions.question: How does river erosion make a virtual reality tour useful for experiencing parts of Majuli River Island that people may no longer be able to visit?
questions.reference_answer: River erosion reduces Majuli's habitable area and can turn former habitable land into sandbars, river banks, underwater areas, or barren areas. Immersive technologies are useful for heritage places that cannot be physically visited in all parts, because they recreate the space as a virtual environment and virtual reality lets a global audience explore heritage remotely without visiting.
